stage_one.quote: The first stage will determine via pass/fail whether the ideas meet a baseline level of viability, in that the Project reasonably fits the theme and reasonably applies the required APIs/SDKs featured in the Hackathon.

gates.requirement: Project reasonably applies the required APIs/SDKs

items.name: Technical Implementation
items.quote: Does the project demonstrate genuine software craftsmanship? Is the chosen AWS Database (Aurora, Aurora DSQL, or DynamoDB) integrated thoughtfully — with a data model, schema, or query design that reflects a deliberate architectural choice?
signals: a deliberate data model, not a default
Vercel deployment beyond a basic setup

items.name: Design
items.quote: Is the user experience intuitive and well-considered? Does the front-end feel designed in relation to the back-end? Is there a cohesive, intentional balance between the two layers that reflects full-stack thinking?
signals: front-end designed in relation to the back-end

items.name: Impact & Real-World Applicability
items.quote: Does the project solve a meaningful problem for a real audience? Does the use of scalable database infrastructure and frontend deployment make the solution more viable — not just functional, but potentially shippable?

items.name: Originality
items.quote: How creative and original is the concept? Does the project demonstrate a genuine insight about what's possible with this stack? If the idea isn't new, how significantly does this implementation push it forward?
signals: a genuine insight about the stack

bonus.required_disclosure: You must include language that says you created the piece of content for the purposes of entering this hackathon.
bonus.quote: Submissions that advance to Stage Two may earn up to 0.6 additional points on top of their score by publishing a piece of content (blog, podcast, video) covering how the project was built using one of the required databases and Vercel on any public platform.

required.name: AWS Database
required.quote: all projects must use one of three designated Amazon Web Services Databases (Aurora, Aurora DSQL, or DynamoDB) as the primary back end

required.name: Vercel or v0.app deployment
required.quote: and deploy their front end on Vercel or v0.app

encouraged.name: v0
encouraged.quote: You must deploy on Vercel, but v0 is one of several ways to do that. v0 is recommended for speed, not required.

judges.name: Aditya Samant
judges.title: Principal Database Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS Databases

panel_read: All ten judges are AWS database leadership — product managers, principal technologists and database specialist solutions architects. The database-architecture story is the strongest card: a deliberate data model, a defensible reason this engine and not another, and evidence the schema was designed rather than generated. Surface it early and everywhere.

notes: Any Judge, or company or individual that employs a Judge, is ineligible
Employees and immediate family of the Sponsor and Administrator are ineligible
eligibility.quote: Individuals who are residents of, or Organizations domiciled in, a country, state, province or territory where the laws of the United States or local law prohibits participating or receiving a prize in the Hackathon

constraints.constraint: Judges may score on the description, images and video alone. The project must be free and unrestricted to test, with credentials supplied if it is private.
constraints.implication: The written submission must stand on its own, and a no-account demo path is a rule rather than a nicety.
constraints.quote: Judges are not required to test the Project and may choose to judge based solely on the text description, images, and video provided in the Submission.

constraints.constraint: A pre-existing project must have adopted the required integration after the submission period opened, and evidence of in-window work may be demanded.
constraints.implication: Keep commit history inside the submission window.
constraints.quote: The administrator and/or the Sponsor reserve the right to request evidence of work completed during the Submission Period; failure to provide may result in disqualification.

constraints.constraint: Each project may be submitted to exactly one track.
constraints.implication: Track choice is a single irreversible bet, so it is made deliberately at :describe.
constraints.quote: Each project can only be submitted to one Track.

constraints.constraint: All submission materials must be in English, or accompanied by an English translation.
constraints.implication: No action needed; noted for completeness.
constraints.quote: All Submission materials must be in English or, if not in English, the Entrant must provide an English translation

host_guidance.guidance: Label every box with both what it is (the component type) and what it does. Show direction of calls with arrows, bidirectional only when it actually is. Group cloud-provider services in a dashed box. The AWS Architecture Icons set and draw.io are recommended.
Using v0, Copilot or Cursor is allowed and encouraged, but submissions with no meaningful engineering decisions will score poorly on Technical Implementation.
A project may use more than one AWS Database; judges evaluate the architecture including the choice of database.
Never commit credentials to the repository, which must be public for review. The Vercel Marketplace OIDC integration is the most secure option — IAM roles with no stored keys.
